title: Forecast many business time series
problem: Regular temporal data and many related series.
rationale: Start with seasonal/statistical baselines in StatsForecast or sktime; evaluate neural forecasting only when data and accuracy gains justify it.
first_step: Use rolling-origin backtests and explicit prediction horizons rather than random train/test splitting.
validation: Measure horizon-specific error, interval coverage, runtime and stability across seasonal regimes.
caveat: Missing timestamps, future covariates and target leakage can dominate model differences.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Train an RL agent in simulation
problem: A task with defined observations, actions, rewards and termination.
rationale: Gymnasium provides the interface; use Stable-Baselines3 for reusable baselines or CleanRL for inspectable implementations; MuJoCo is optional physics.
first_step: Validate environment dynamics with a scripted policy and a random-policy baseline before learning.
validation: Report multiple seeds, true objective metrics, reward exploits and performance on changed conditions.
caveat: High simulated return does not guarantee real-world safety or transfer; rewards can be misspecified.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Use sensitive data with privacy accounting
problem: A task requiring a formal privacy mechanism, not just anonymized columns.
rationale: Choose Opacus or TensorFlow Privacy for compatible private training; Presidio helps detect sensitive text; Flower is a separate federation option.
first_step: Define the threat model, accounting assumptions and acceptable utility loss before training.
validation: Audit the privacy accountant, sampling assumptions, clipping settings, leakage paths and utility tradeoff.
caveat: Federated learning and identifier removal do not automatically provide differential privacy or compliance.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Build a durable tool-using workflow
problem: Multi-step tasks need explicit state, review and recovery.
rationale: Use LangGraph for stateful model workflows, typed validation where helpful, and Temporal only when cross-service durable execution warrants it.
first_step: Build a narrow graph with tool allowlists, approval points and safe failure behavior.
validation: Inject timeouts, duplicate events and bad tool output; verify idempotency, authorization and recoverability.
caveat: LLM instructions are not a security boundary; tool permissions and resource budgets must be enforced externally.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Explore graph or scientific models
problem: A structural or mathematical problem where a generic chat model is not the right core.
rationale: Choose graph tooling for explicit relational structure, probabilistic programming for uncertainty models, or differentiable solvers for dynamics.
first_step: Write down the modeling assumptions and build the smallest synthetic case with a known answer.
validation: Compare with a simple numerical or statistical baseline and test calibration or solver accuracy as applicable.
caveat: These tools solve different problem classes; they are alternative starting points, not one universal science stack.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested
